subject: Environment
description: First Indian Ramsar site, count, state-site matching, recent additions, Montreux register

options.option_text: Wular Lake
Chilika Lake (Odisha)
Sundarbans
Loktak

questions.explanation: Chilika and Keoladeo NP — both designated India's first two Ramsar sites on 1 October 1981 (joint first). Chilika is the largest brackish-water lagoon in India. Keoladeo (Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary) was the second designated, but Chilika is mentioned first in chronology by some references. Wular followed in 1990. India joined Ramsar Convention 1 February 1982 (delayed; sites were designated even before formal accession).
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: As of early 2026, the approximate number of Ramsar sites in India is:

options.option_text: 85+ (most in Asia; second-largest globally after UK in some count)

questions.explanation: India has 85+ Ramsar sites (latest additions in 2024-25). Largest network in Asia; UK / Mexico are the only other countries with comparable counts. Tamil Nadu has the most (16+), followed by Uttar Pradesh and Gujarat. Total area covered ~13 lakh hectares (~1.5% of India's land). Pace of addition has accelerated greatly since 2020 — government's commitment under SDG 6 + 15. Original 1981 sites: Chilika, Keoladeo. World Wetlands Day: 2 February.
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: Match the Ramsar site with its state — which pairing is INCORRECT?

options.option_text: Sambhar Salt Lake — Rajasthan
Pong Dam Lake — Punjab
Vembanad-Kol — Kerala
Pulicat — Andhra Pradesh / Tamil Nadu

questions.explanation: Pong Dam Lake is in HIMACHAL PRADESH (Kangra district, on Beas river) — NOT Punjab. Designated Ramsar 2002. Hosts ~70,000+ migratory waterfowl every winter. Sambhar — Rajasthan (largest inland salt lake). Vembanad-Kol — Kerala (longest lake). Pulicat — AP-TN border (lighthouse located in TN side). Other major Ramsar sites — Loktak (Manipur), Wular (J&K), Sundarbans (WB), Sundarban Mangroves (WB), Renuka (HP), Tsomoriri (Ladakh), Bhitarkanika (Odisha).
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: Currently on the 'Montreux Record' (Ramsar sites with adverse ecological change), India has:

options.option_text: 5 sites
2 sites — Keoladeo NP (Rajasthan) and Loktak Lake (Manipur)
0 sites
10 sites

questions.explanation: Montreux Record (1990 onwards) lists Ramsar sites where ecological character is at threat. India has TWO entries — Keoladeo NP (water shortage, drying) and Loktak Lake (siltation, Ithai barrage damming, phumdi proliferation). Chilika was on it (1993) but REMOVED in 2002 after successful restoration — only the third site in the world to be removed from the Record. Listing is voluntary (the country must request); India listed Keoladeo and Loktak in 1990 and 1993 respectively.
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: Which is India's largest Ramsar site by area?

options.option_text: Chilika
Sundarbans Wetland (West Bengal)
Vembanad-Kol
Wular

questions.explanation: Sundarbans Wetland (designated 2019) — area ~4,230 km² — India's largest Ramsar site. Part of the world's largest contiguous mangrove forest. Important habitat for the Royal Bengal Tiger (saltwater swimmers) and Estuarine crocodile. Other large Ramsar sites in India — Vembanad-Kol (~1,512 km²), Chilika (~1,165 km²). Smallest Ramsar in India — Renuka (HP, just 0.2 km²). Largest in the world — Rio Negro (Brazil, 12+ million ha), Queen Maud Gulf (Canada).
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: Tsomoriri / Tsomori Lake — a high-altitude Ramsar site (4,522 m) in Ladakh — is famous for hosting the only breeding population of the:

options.option_text: Sarus Crane
Bar-headed Goose (Anser indicus)
Greater Adjutant Stork
Pelican

questions.explanation: Tsomoriri — designated Ramsar 2002. Holds India's only known breeding population of Bar-headed Goose — a record holder for highest altitude bird migration (crosses Himalayas at >7,000 m). Also breeds Black-necked Crane (Tibetan crane), Brown-headed Gull. Tso Kar (also Ladakh, designated 2020) is a sister site. Greater Adjutant — Assam (Boragaon Wetland, Deepor Beel). Sarus crane — Bharatpur, Etawah. Pelicans — Pulicat, Kolleru, Nelapattu.
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: The state with the highest number of Ramsar sites in India is:

options.option_text: Maharashtra
Tamil Nadu (16+ sites)
West Bengal
Kerala

questions.explanation: Tamil Nadu — most Ramsar sites (16+) including Chitrangudi, Kanjirankulam, Karaivetti, Karikili, Pallikaranai (Chennai's last large urban wetland), Pichavaram (mangroves), Point Calimere, Suchindram-Theroor, Vaduvur, Vedanthangal (oldest bird sanctuary in India, 1858), Vellode, Vembannur, Udhayamarthandapuram, Sakkarakottai, Long-Wood Shola, Karaivetti. UP — 11+, Gujarat — 4. The recent (2022) Ramsar push expanded TN's count significantly.
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: Loktak Lake in Manipur, a Ramsar site since 1990, is home to the world's only floating national park. What is that national park called?

options.option_text: Keibul Lamjao National Park, floating on phumdis biomass
Nokrek National Park, on the Garo Hills plateau in Meghalaya
Manas National Park, spanning the Assam-Bhutan foothills region
Dampa Tiger Reserve, located in the Lushai Hills of Mizoram

questions.explanation: Keibul Lamjao National Park is the world's only floating national park, situated on the phumdis — heterogeneous floating masses of vegetation, soil, and organic matter — of Loktak Lake. It is also the last natural refuge of the endangered Sangai deer (Cervus eldi eldi). Nokrek and Manas are entirely different Northeast parks with no connection to Loktak.

questions.stem: Keoladeo Ghana National Park (Bharatpur), co-designated as India's first Ramsar site in 1981, was originally created in the 19th century as what type of facility?

options.option_text: A bird-breeding centre to rehabilitate endangered migratory cranes
A flood-diversion channel for managing Yamuna river overflow waters
A royal duck-hunting reserve for British viceroys and Indian princes
A freshwater reservoir for irrigating agricultural lands near Bharatpur

questions.explanation: Keoladeo was created by constructing the Ajan Bund in 1899 by the rulers of Bharatpur as a private duck-shooting reserve hosting grand shoots for British Viceroys and Indian royalty. It became a national park in 1982 and a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985. Option A (crane rehabilitation) is a classic distractor — the famous Siberian crane visits were a natural phenomenon, not the park's original purpose.

questions.stem: Harike Wetland in Punjab — the largest wetland in northern India and a Ramsar site since 1990 — is formed at the confluence of which two rivers?

options.option_text: The Ravi and the Chenab rivers, near Pathankot in northern Punjab
The Beas and the Sutlej rivers, near Ferozepur district in Punjab
The Ghaggar and the Yamuna rivers, at the Haryana-Punjab border region
The Jhelum and the Chenab rivers, in the upper Indus plains of Punjab

questions.explanation: Harike Wetland (also called Hari-ke-Pattan) lies just downstream of the confluence of the Beas and Sutlej rivers in Ferozepur and Tarn Taran districts of Punjab. Option A (Ravi-Chenab) is a plausible distractor as both are major Punjab rivers, but they do not form Harike. Option C is wrong because the Ghaggar and Yamuna meet nowhere near Punjab's Harike.

questions.stem: Sambhar Salt Lake in Rajasthan, India's largest inland saline lake and a Ramsar site, is economically significant primarily as one of India's largest inland sources of which product?

options.option_text: Sodium carbonate (soda ash), supplied to the Indian glass industry
Sodium chloride (common salt), as one of India's largest inland sources
Potassium nitrate (saltpeter), historically used in India's gunpowder
Magnesium sulfate (Epsom salt), used in pharmaceutical manufacturing

questions.explanation: Sambhar Salt Lake produces sodium chloride (common salt) and has been a major inland salt source for centuries. Salt production here is managed by Sambhar Salts Ltd. Option A (soda ash / sodium carbonate) is the most tempting distractor — many candidates confuse 'saline/soda lake' with soda ash production, but Sambhar's primary output is NaCl, not Na₂CO₃.

questions.stem: Deepor Beel in Assam, a Ramsar site on the western outskirts of Guwahati city, faces a combination of threats most directly linked to its urban location. Which of the following is the MOST documented urban-specific threat to this site?

options.option_text: Rampant sand-mining from the lakebed by commercial contractors
A railway track cutting through it alongside municipal solid-waste dumping
Oil-spill contamination from an adjacent petroleum refinery outfall canal
Uncontrolled commercial fishing rapidly depleting its native fish diversity

questions.explanation: Deepor Beel faces two well-documented urban-origin threats: (1) the Northeast Frontier Railway line physically cuts through the wetland, fragmenting habitat and blocking elephant corridors; and (2) Guwahati city dumps municipal solid waste on its margins, causing severe eutrophication. A refinery outfall and rampant sand-mining are associated with other Assamese wetlands but are not the primary documented threats at Deepor Beel.

questions.stem: Lonar Lake in Maharashtra, added to the Ramsar list in 2020, is scientifically unique as one of only four confirmed hyper-velocity meteorite impact craters globally formed in which type of geological substrate?

options.option_text: Basaltic rock of the Deccan Traps, a large igneous province formation
Crystalline granite of the Archean Peninsular Gneissic basement complex
Sedimentary limestone layers of the Vindhyan Supergroup stratified rocks
Metamorphic quartzite layers within the Eastern Ghats mobile belt zone

questions.explanation: Lonar Lake is geologically extraordinary because it formed in the basaltic rock of the Deccan Traps — nearly all other confirmed hyper-velocity impact craters worldwide occur in ancient crystalline (granite/gneiss) rock. Option B (Peninsular granite) is the most tempting distractor since the Indian Shield underlies much of the peninsula and is the expected substrate for old craters. Lonar's unique basalt substrate also gives the lake its rare saline-alkaline chemistry.

questions.stem: Bhitarkanika Mangroves in Odisha — India's second-largest mangrove ecosystem and a Ramsar site since 2002 — holds which of the following distinctions that makes it especially critical to Indian wildlife conservation?

options.option_text: It supports India's largest known population of saltwater crocodiles
It is the sole remaining breeding habitat of the Gangetic river dolphin
It holds the only documented nesting colony of greater adjutant storks
It has the highest recorded fishing-cat density in any Indian wetland

questions.explanation: Bhitarkanika harbours India's largest population of saltwater crocodiles (Crocodylus porosus), a Schedule I species, making it the flagship site for Indian crocodile conservation. Option B is wrong: Gangetic river dolphins inhabit riverine habitats across the Ganga-Brahmaputra system, not mangrove estuaries. Option C is wrong: greater adjutant storks nest primarily in Assam's Brahmaputra floodplain villages (Dadara, Pacharia), not at Bhitarkanika.
